Symbol Dictionary

¶10. As in the Days of Noah — the Last Mingling

Section 10 of 12 · ≈17 min

In This Section

Christ appointed BOTH Genesis judgments — the flood and Sodom — as one picture of the last age: lawful things made the whole of life, the covenant line mingled with the world until "knew not," and sudden separation by judgment "the same day" the righteous go out; the last mingling is not out in the world but inside the church, and against it the old calls of separation sound again as present truth.

Christ appoints the FIRST Genesis judgment as the picture of the last age — Luke 17:26-27; Matt. 24:37-39:

  • Luke 17:26. "And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man" — Christ Himself fixes the type: the antediluvian world is the mirror of the last generation. He does not reach for a new figure; He reaches back to the first judgment.
    • the days of the Son of man = the last age, defined by Christ Himself through the matched Noah/Lot pattern — heedless absorption in lawful things ("they did eat, they drank... bought... sold... planted... builded"), mingled worship as the covenant line blends with the world, and sudden separation by judgment on "the same day" the righteous go out; the mark is not open rebellion but "knew not" (Luke 17:26-30; Matt. 24:37-39; Gen. 6:2, 5; Gen. 13:12-13). Defined in full in the Symbol Dictionary.
  • Luke 17:27. "They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all" — four verbs, every one lawful. Eating, drinking, and marrying made the whole of life right up to the day of separation; not one open crime is named — the indictment is absorption.
  • Matt. 24:37. "But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be." — the parallel account fixes the same appointment; the days of Noah are not an illustration but a stated equivalence.
  • Matt. 24:38-39. "they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage... And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be" — the diagnosis in two words: "knew not." Heedlessness, not defiance, is the mark of the age (eating and drinking as the mark of the heedless class is defined in “The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack”).
  • WitnessDA 633.1. White: "Christ continues, pointing out the condition of the world at His coming: 'As the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be'... He tells us that as it was in Noah's day, so will it be when the Son of man comes again." — confirms that the Noah saying is Christ's own definition of the state of the world at His coming, not merely its suddenness.
  • WitnessAH 121.3. White: "There is in itself no sin in eating and drinking, or in marrying and giving in marriage... But in the days of Noah men married without consulting God..." — the precise edge of the charge: the condemned things were LAWFUL, carried on without God until they became the whole of life.

The SECOND judgment added as a matched pair — the days of Lot — Luke 17:28-30:

  • Luke 17:28. "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded" — six verbs now: to the antediluvian four Christ adds buying, selling, planting, building — the busy commerce of the city. The last age is pictured as uninterrupted business.
  • Luke 17:29-30. "But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all. Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed" — "the same day": the going out of the righteous and the fall of judgment are one event, as at the ark door. The commerce runs to the very hour.
  • WitnessCD 17.6. White: "Our Saviour warned His disciples that just prior to His second coming a state of things would exist very similar to that which preceded the flood. Eating and drinking would be carried to excess... more and more like the doomed inhabitants of Sodom" — joins BOTH judgments, flood and Sodom, as one last-days picture of appetite and pleasure — exactly Luke 17's pairing.
  • WitnessCD 435.2. White: "The world's Redeemer, who knows well the state of society in the last days, represents eating and drinking as the sins that condemn this age" — names the lawful-made-ultimate as the condemning sin of the age, per the Noah pattern.

What "the days of Noah" actually were — the mingling behind the meals — Gen. 6:2, 5:

  • Gen. 6:2. "That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" — behind the eating and marrying stood the MINGLING: the covenant line of Seth blended with the line of Cain, and the distinction dissolved (the sons of God, the daughters of men, and the mingling are defined in “The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity”). The attack fell on the Eden institution of marriage.
  • Gen. 6:5. "And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" — the result once the two classes blended: universal corruption. The mingling, not merely open sin, produced the world the flood swept away.
  • WitnessPP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate... So long as this separation continued, they maintained the worship of God in its purity. But in the lapse of time they ventured, little by little, to mingle with the inhabitants of the valleys... and they lost their peculiar, holy character" — the master witness: separation maintained the pure worship, and gradual mingling — "little by little" — dissolved the peculiar character. THIS is the substance of "as it was in the days of Noe."
  • WitnessPP 85.4. White: Enoch, "fearing that their infidelity might lessen his reverence for God... avoided constant association with them, and spent much time in solitude, giving himself to meditation and prayer" — the counter-example inside the same generation: deliberate separation from the mingled society preserved the walk with God.

The last mingling is from INSIDE — a form of godliness, Laodicea at ease — 2 Tim. 3:1-5; Rev. 3:17:

  • 2 Tim. 3:1-2. "This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous..." — Paul dates the catalogue "in the last days," and the peril is a character-list, not a persecution-list: the danger comes from what men LOVE.
  • 2 Tim. 3:4-5. "lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away" — the crisis of the list: these are the PROFESSED. The Noah/Lot mingling is relocated from the world into the church — appetite and pleasure ruling under an exterior of piety — and the command is still separation: "from such turn away."
    • having a form of godliness = the last-days condition inside the church: an outward shape of religion emptied of its power, the professed mingled with the world in appetite and pleasure while keeping the exterior of piety — the Noah/Lot mingling moved from the world into the sanctuary (2 Tim. 3:1-5; Rev. 3:17; Matt. 24:39). Defined in full in the Symbol Dictionary.
  • Rev. 3:17. "Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked" — Laodicea: the church at ease in the city, and — like the antediluvians — "knowest not." The days-of-Noah heedlessness has entered the sanctuary.
  • WitnessCOL 158.3. White: "The Lord says, 'Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing...' The gold tried in the fire is faith that works by love" — applies Rev. 3:17 to the church's self-satisfied wealth; the remedy is not more goods but tried faith.
  • WitnessMYP 390.2. White: "The eternal God has drawn the line of distinction between the saint and the sinner... The two classes do not blend into each other imperceptibly, like the colors of a rainbow, but are as distinct as midday and midnight" — carries the two-classes line into the end time, and names the modern mingling precisely: "God's people cannot with safety enter into intimate associations with those who know the truth, but do not practice it."

Against it, the old calls sound again — out of the cities — Gen. 13:12-13; CH 268.1:

  • Gen. 13:12-13. "Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelled in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom. But the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the LORD exceedingly" — the two-classes divergence in one verse: Abraham in the pilgrim land, Lot drifting cityward while the city's wickedness is named in the same breath (the tent-and-altar life and the plain of Sodom are defined in “Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain”).
  • WitnessPP 168.1. White: "In how wide contrast to the life of Abraham was that of Lot! Once they had been companions, worshiping at one altar... Lot had chosen Sodom for its pleasure and profit... he had permitted his children to mingle with a corrupt and idolatrous people" — the narrative of the drift: one altar shared, then the city chosen for pleasure and profit, and the children lost to mingling.
  • WitnessCH 268.1. White: "'Out of the cities,' is my message... I hope and pray and believe that they will now arouse to the importance of getting out into the country" — the present-truth reissue of the old separations: her repeated turn-of-the-century "Out of the cities" appeals reissued the antediluvian separation as present truth for the last generation — the modern tent-pitching.
  • WitnessCL 5.2. White: "Parents flock with their families to the cities, because they fancy it easier to obtain a livelihood there... they stay where they are, until Satan gains full control of their children" — the modern Lot-toward-Sodom drift named: cityward for livelihood, exactly as Lot chose the plain, and the children lost to the mingling exactly as in Sodom.
  • John 4:21, 23-24. "neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem... the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth... God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth" — the call out of the city costs no worship: Christ de-localizes it. The peculiar people are bound to no city or temple; they carry the true worship with them, as Abraham carried his altar.

The return toward the Eden table — Gen. 1:29:

  • Gen. 1:29. "Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat" — the original grant, one of the institutions of Eden with marriage and the Sabbath (the institutions of Eden and the original diet are defined in “The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack”); flesh was not granted until after the flood (Gen. 9:3).
  • WitnessEv 663.4. White: "In the beginning, fruit was pronounced by God as 'good for food.' The permission to eat flesh meat was a consequence of the fall. Not till after the Flood was man given permission to eat the flesh of animals" — anchors the health message to Genesis: Gen. 1:29 the original table, flesh a post-fall, post-flood concession.
  • WitnessCG 383.1. White: "Is it not time that all should aim to dispense with flesh foods?... Let them, rather, return to the wholesome and delicious food given to man in the beginning" — the reform framed explicitly as a RETURN toward Eden's institution: not salvation by menu, but the peculiar people re-learning the institutions of Eden while the world perfects the way of Cain (see “Cain and Abel — the Two Worships”).

The last-generation text — Remember Lot's wife — Luke 17:32; Gen. 19:26:

  • Luke 17:32. "Remember Lot's wife." — three words, Christ's own memorial nailed into the days-of-the-Son-of-man discourse itself. The warning is not against staying in the city; she had left it. It is against a divided leaving of it — a separation of the feet without a separation of the heart.
    • Remember Lot's wife = the last-generation warning against a divided separation — out of the city with the body, in it with the heart; she obeyed the call to come out, and one backward look fixed her forever as the standing type of the professor whose separation never reached the affections (Luke 17:32; Gen. 19:26; Gen. 13:12-13). Defined in full in the Symbol Dictionary.
  • Gen. 19:26. "But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt" — the literal fate the command points back to: her feet left Sodom, her heart lingered, and the lingering look was fatal. Separation of the body without separation of the heart is no separation at all.

Synthesis

DEFINITION — AS IN THE DAYS OF NOAH — THE LAST MINGLING = Christ appointed both Genesis judgments as one picture of the last age: "as it was in the days of Noe... likewise also as it was in the days of Lot" (Luke 17:26-30; Matt. 24:37-39) — lawful things made the whole of life ("they did eat, they drank, they married wives... they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded"), carried on "until the day" the righteous went out and judgment fell "the same day," with the fatal diagnosis "knew not." Behind the antediluvian meals and marriages stood the mingling: the sons of God took the daughters of men (Gen. 6:2), the two classes blended, "every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" (Gen. 6:5) — for "so long as this separation continued, they maintained the worship of God in its purity," and mingling "little by little" cost them their "peculiar, holy character" (PP 81.2). The last generation meets this same mingling from INSIDE the profession: "lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof" (2 Tim. 3:1-5), Laodicea "rich, and increased with goods... and knowest not" (Rev. 3:17) — the church at ease in the city, distinct from the world "as midday and midnight" in God's intent (MYP 390.2) yet blending in fact. Against it the old calls of Eden and of Abraham sound again as present truth: "'Out of the cities,' is my message" (CH 268.1; CL 5.2) — the modern tent-pitching against the modern drift toward the plain (Gen. 13:12-13; PP 168.1) — and the return toward the Eden table of Gen. 1:29 (Ev 663.4; CG 383.1), the peculiar people re-learning the institutions of Eden while the world perfects the way of Cain, carrying worship "in spirit and in truth" out of every city (John 4:21-24). And over the whole age stands Christ's shortest sermon: "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32; Gen. 19:26) — for the days of the Son of man end as Noah's and Lot's did, in sudden separation by judgment, and the only separation that survives it is one of the heart. The two classes here re-formed become fully and finally visible in the seal and the mark (see “The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible”), under the last form of the old call: "Come out of her, my people" (see “Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call”).

Symbols Defined Here

  • the days of the Son of man = the last age, defined by Christ through the matched Noah/Lot pattern — heedless absorption in lawful things (eating, drinking, marrying, buying, selling, planting, building), mingled worship as the covenant line blends with the world, and sudden separation by judgment on "the same day" the righteous go out; the mark of the age is "knew not" (Luke 17:26-30; Matt. 24:37-39; Gen. 6:2, 5; Gen. 13:12-13).
  • Remember Lot's wife = the last-generation warning against a divided separation — out of the city with the body, in it with the heart; she obeyed the call to come out, and one backward look fixed her forever as the standing type of the professor whose separation never reached the affections (Luke 17:32; Gen. 19:26; Gen. 13:12-13).
  • having a form of godliness = the last-days condition inside the church: an outward shape of religion emptied of its power, the professed mingled with the world in appetite and pleasure while keeping the exterior of piety — the Noah/Lot mingling relocated from the world into the sanctuary, Laodicea "rich, and increased with goods" yet "knowest not" (2 Tim. 3:1-5; Rev. 3:17; Matt. 24:39).

Symbols Carried

the mingling, the sons of God, and the daughters of men — the mechanism by which the peculiar people lose their peculiarity (see “The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity”); the institutions of Eden, the original diet, and eating and drinking as the mark of the heedless class (see “The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack”); the tent and the altar, the plain of Sodom, and the pilgrim identity behind the out-of-the-cities call (see “Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain”); the peculiar people (see "Israel Mingles — 'Like All the Nations'"); the way of Cain, the self-chosen worship the world perfects while the remnant returns to the appointed way (see “Cain and Abel — the Two Worships”); the two classes made finally visible in seal and mark (see “The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible”); and the last call out of the city (see “Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call”).

For Discussion

  1. Every verb in Christ's picture of the last age is lawful — "they did eat, they drank... they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded" (Luke 17:27-28) — and the fatal word is "knew not" (Matt. 24:39). Where in your own life has a lawful thing quietly become the whole of life — and how would you find out, given that the very mark of this condition is not knowing?
  2. Paul locates the last mingling inside the profession — "a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof" (2 Tim. 3:5) — and Laodicea says "I am rich... and knowest not" (Rev. 3:17), while PP 81.2 says the two classes were safe only "so long as this separation continued" and fell "little by little." What does the Sethites' little-by-little descent to the valleys look like among us now — in associations, in appetite, in what we love (MYP 390.2)?
  3. "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32): she was already out of Sodom in body when the look destroyed her (Gen. 19:26). If the calls out of the city and back toward the Eden table (CH 268.1; Gen. 1:29) were obeyed only in address and menu, what would be gained? What would a separation of the heart — not merely of the feet — look like for you this week?
